definition: Diathesis is a constitutional predisposition that makes a person especially liable to a particular disease. In historical psychology and psychiatry, it was also used for an inherited or degenerative mental disposition thought to increase vulnerability to insanity or milder mental irregularity.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Diathesis; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports a degenerative mental disposition, but it does not support the added claim that this disposition was inherited.
The rest of the definition is broadly supported, but the unsupported inherited component makes the definition too expansive for the source.
The definition claims diathesis was “inherited” as well as degenerative; the packet discusses it as “degenerate diathesis” and “brain deterioration,” but it does not explicitly state “inherited.”

The second sentence also adds the phrasing “in historical psychology and psychiatry” as a stated usage scope; while the packet notes extensive use with reference to mental conditions, it does not explicitly frame it in exactly those terms.
